# 2 Clement Chapter 19 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET / LOGOS / PNEUMA

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "reading... an exhortation" vs. the preacher's self-description
- EMET: "I am reading to you an exhortation"
- LOGOS: "I read you an exhortation"
- PNEUMA: "I am reading you this exhortation"
- **Ruling:** "I read you an exhortation" — present tense is appropriate for the performative reading moment; the preacher is describing the act as it happens.

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "goal" vs. "foundation" vs. "lay down a goal"
- EMET: "we shall set a goal for all the young people"
- LOGOS: "we will lay down a goal for all the young"
- PNEUMA: "we will lay a foundation for all the young people"
- **Ruling:** "we will lay down a goal for all the young" — *hypeuthymon stēsomen* means "we will set up a responsibility/standard"; "foundation" (PNEUMA) imports building imagery; "goal" is acceptable.

## Disagreement 3 — v.5: "pluck the immortal fruit" vs. "gather the immortal fruit" vs. "harvest"
- EMET: "gather the immortal fruit of the resurrection"
- LOGOS: "pluck the immortal fruit of the resurrection"
- PNEUMA: "harvest the undying fruit of the resurrection"
- **Ruling:** "pluck the immortal fruit of the resurrection" — *trygēsousin ton athanaton karpon* — *trygaō* is specifically to pick/pluck ripe fruit at harvest; "pluck" best captures this.

## Disagreement 4 — v.7: "with those who have revived above" vs. "with those who have been raised" vs. "with the fathers who have been revived"
- EMET: "with those who have revived above"
- LOGOS: "with the fathers who have been revived"
- PNEUMA: "with those who have already been raised"
- **Ruling:** "with those who have been raised" — *meta tōn anazēsantōn* — "those who have come to life again" without specifying "fathers" (LOGOS adds) or "above" (EMET adds); PNEUMA is closest but changes the aorist to perfect.

## Disagreement 5 — v.7: "world that does not die" vs. "world that knows no grief"
- EMET: "world that does not die"
- LOGOS: "world that knows no grief"
- PNEUMA: "world that never ends"
- **Ruling:** "world that knows no grief" — *aiōna ton alypōn* — *alypos* means "free from grief/pain," not "undying"; EMET and PNEUMA misread the term; LOGOS is correct.

**Total disagreements: 5**
